summary: The weakest batch of the campaign so far, and clearly written tired. Commons and Uncommons are mostly fine, real habits (the pen-ink ring, the bucket crack in a shoe, the vending machine that rejects a coin five times, the bath tap that goes from cold to boiling). From Rare up, though, almost every object either does its job well (cools a room, blends fast, keeps tea warm) or scales one trait (water tank noises, towel piles, ironing-board collapses). Epics are quiet family scenes or crowds, and Legendaries are pleasant successes or 'for N years' lines. All 93 Legendary names are 'The X That Y'. Move names are mostly truthful, but heat names are pasted onto cold glassware ('Clink Heat', 'Shake Heat'), the fridge kit is left on ovens, irons and radiators, and 22 Ultimates repeat the Epic. Sensitive: the shot glass's medicine-measuring Uncommon and Legendary must go; the other alcohol-free drinkware is fine. Every high and medium item has a fresh replacement, and the name swaps were checked for length, ASCII and uniqueness across all content and the Pilot 01 proposal.

patterns.pattern: Rare is the object doing its job (cools, blends, pours, brews, scrubs, dries) rather than a troublesome power (82 of 93 Rares are flagged).
patterns.suggestion: Replacement Rares are given for each listed object; every one is a power that causes trouble (Icebrow, Spoonhoarder, Loyalbrew, Wishpour, Shrinkheater).

patterns.pattern: Epics are quiet everyday incidents or crowd scenes ('fed a whole family', 'the whole kitchen', 'every child on the street got soaked') with no concrete consequence or joke.
patterns.suggestion: Each listed Epic gets one concrete consequence with a punchline (the house pushed into the shade, the ice-cream van floating down the high street, the long jump becoming the long swim).

patterns.pattern: Legendaries are pleasant successes or 'for N years / so many times / never once / without ever' lines (88 of 93 Legendaries are flagged); all 93 Legendary names start 'The X That/Who/With...'.
patterns.suggestion: Replacement Legendaries are outrageous feats with punchlines, and their paired names use 'Name, the Epithet', single names and titles; after the swaps 'The X That' drops to 5 of 93. About 15 of 93 replacement Legendaries are cosmic, under the one-third limit.

patterns.pattern: Fridge and kettle kit defaults left on objects they do not fit: 'Frost Breath', 'Ice Cube Barrage' and 'Cold Storage' on the oven, iron, radiator, ironing board, rotisserie, foot spa, range hood and sewing machine table; 'Caffeine Kick' on the flute, cocktail shaker and gravy boat; 'Boiling Broth' and 'Noodle Whip' on cereal, granola and coleslaw.
patterns.suggestion: Rename the kit slot for these objects only (names given). Kit names that fit, such as 'Frost Breath' on the air conditioner, stay.

patterns.pattern: Signature heat template: 'Hot X Heat' (Hot Tea Heat x4, Hot Sip Heat x3, Hot Pour Heat x3, Hot Broth Heat x3, Hot Rice Heat x3, Hot Cheese Heat x2) and heat names on cold glassware ('Clink Heat', 'Shake Heat', 'Hot Clink Heat', 'Hot Juice Heat', 'Crunch Heat' on cereal and coleslaw).
patterns.suggestion: Cold drinks get a believable heat image (sunbeam through glass, ginger, cocoa, mustard). The generic templates are listed as low, each with an object-specific name.

patterns.pattern: Ultimate repeats or contains the Epic name in 22 objects (Festival Clink, Washing Up Hero, Playground Splash, Late Night Slurp, Takeaway Night, Bowl Avalanche).
patterns.suggestion: Each finisher gets its own image; varied Ultimates are effect-neutral.

patterns.pattern: One trait scaled over three or four rarities instead of a new premise per rarity: water tank (noises), towel rack (holding towels), ironing board (collapsing), rotisserie (people watching), humidifier (mist), creamer (swirls), noodles (one long noodle), radiator (socks).
patterns.suggestion: Replacements give each rarity its own premise.

patterns.pattern: Cluster tell-apart. Cups: mug = owner's mug; bone china = posh manners; teacup and saucer = tea leaves and rattling; tea set = visitors; camping mug = dents and squirrels; enamel mug = woodsmoke; espresso = speed; soup mug = flavours; travel cup = commute; takeaway cup = misspelled names. Glasses: glass = refilling; juice glass = breakfast and sunrise; milk glass = moustache and strength; flute = floating bubbles; martini glass = blue drinks and balance; shot glass = tiny size; tumbler = rolling; stein = lid; tankard = huzzah and lookout. Bowls: noodles = long noodle; pho = herbs and fogged glasses; ramen = egg and whistle. Oatmeal = swelling and setting hard; porridge = the three bears.
patterns.suggestion: The per-object replacements follow this split.

patterns.pattern: Cross-object copies: ring stains (fountain pen ink U, coffee cup C, juice glass C, mug C); knocked-over glasses (glass U, flute U, juice glass U and E); steam fogging the kitchen (dishwasher, iron); lids flying off and painting the ceiling (blender, cocktail shaker); the little finger in the air (bone china R = tea cup and saucer R, near martini R); cakes wobbling from clinks (flute E = tea cup E); dripping taps (sink C = bath tap U); 'spoon stands up' (coffee machine R, oatmeal E, porridge E); the smoke alarm (air purifier E = range hood E).
patterns.suggestion: One side keeps the premise and the other gets a new one (replacements given).

patterns.pattern: Sensitive objects. Shot glass: the Uncommon (measuring cough syrup) and the Legendary (measuring medicine for the family) are unsafe medicine framing and must go; the name 'Medicine Measure' and the toast Ultimate go too. Alcohol-free drinkware is otherwise handled well (flute, martini, tankard, stein, tumbler and shaker hold juice and milkshake). The teapot's 'Royal Tea' brings in royalty. Also checked: the bidet stays gentle, and the plunger and toilet brush stay clean.
patterns.suggestion: Replacements given. The shot glass now joins the tiny-glass jokes (egg cup confusion, spider bungalow, pocket storm).
